# `get_control_value`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Read one camera control by name (value, type, and radio choices).

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / established (64-bit and 32-bit builds) |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0xf5660, GetControlVal @0x11d7f0, camera GetControlVal @0x1546f0 (64-bit build) |

Reads the named control under the camera mutex. Despite being a read, the 64-bit build can write diagnostic logging state and, for the Temperature control on a main-process build, sends an internal request to the peer processor (internal id 9101) and updates pending-request bookkeeping; a failed relay only drops value_wide. While that relay waits for its reply, the connection handler can run the peer-connect callback, which sends an internal set_local_storage_info request that updates the local storage record; this is why the tier is C on the 64-bit main process. Tier B describes only the local route that runs no such callback; the 32-bit build was not reassessed and stays B. For exact-case TargetTemp the reply value is the cached target temperature. Alternate casings still resolve the control but skip that override.

Side effects: Writes shared logging state/files (Temperature) and, on the 64-bit main process for Temperature, shared pending-request and transport bookkeeping, and the relay wait can trigger a peer-connect callback that updates the local storage record (tier C, 64-bit main process). No camera setting changes.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"get_control_value"`. [READ] |
| `params` | object\|array | yes | - | Control name and an optional items flag, as an object {name, items} or a positional array [name, items]. `name` is required (a missing or non-string name gives 107, although the message reads expected object param) and is matched case-insensitively against the camera's controls. `items` only matters for radio controls with a non-empty item list: the handler tests the raw payload for nonzero without checking the JSON type, so boolean or integer 0 suppresses the list and 1 enables it; behaviour for other types is not established and strict boolean validation must not be assumed. Default: items absent (not emitted). [READ] |

## Reply

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jsonrpc` | string | no | - | (error) Added by the socket layer (reply object constructor), not the handler fragment. Normally present; absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply. Receivers MUST NOT require it. Fixed value `"2.0"`. [READ; also OBSERVED on the wire (2026-10-12)] |
| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (error) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). On events it is always written by the event constructor. [READ; wire shape also OBSERVED (2026-10-12)] |
| `method` | string | if the request had an id and a string method (handler errors and 103), except a locally built stop_func relay failure | - | (error) The request method, echoed. Absent on dispatcher errors 100 and 200 and on a stop_func relay failure. [READ] |
| `error` | string | yes | - | (error) Message looked up from the code; unknown codes yield "fail to operate". [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (error) Nonzero. A requested code of 0 is coerced to 207. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (error) The request id echoed with its JSON type; null on dispatcher errors 100 and 200, where it is the only way to recognise the reply and cannot be matched to a request. [READ] |

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 107 | name missing or not a string (including absent, null or scalar params) | `expected object param` |
| 109 | No available control matches the name | `unexpected param` |
| 318 | Camera absent or closed, or negative camera id | `device not connected` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: method missing or not a string | `invalid request` |

Further numeric-control read errors are unresolved. Camera library return codes are internal and never reach the wire. Units are fixed per control (exposure microseconds, INFERRED; temperature tenths of a degree C; target temperature degrees C; gain tenths of a dB on multiplicative-gain sensors; READ, camera library); see viewing-and-exposure R17b.

## Example

Request, temperature:

```json
{"id":60,"method":"get_control_value","params":{"name":"temperature"}}
```

Reply, ok-number - Numeric control (value invented; shape INFERRED from the documented branch):

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"get_control_value","result":{"name":"temperature","type":"number","value":31.5},"code":0,"id":60}
```

Reply, unknown:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"get_control_value","error":"unexpected param","code":109,"id":61}
```
